content: Lansoprazole is a medication used to treat conditions caused by excessive stomach acid, such as heartburn, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), ulcers, and erosive esophagitis. It is also used to manage conditions where the stomach produces too much acid and to treat infections caused by Helicobacter pylori. Lansoprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Common Side Effects: The most common side effects of lansoprazole include diarrhea, stomach pain, nausea, and constipation. If these symptoms persist or worsen, consult your healthcare provider. Serious Side Effects: 1. Kidney Problems: Acute interstitial nephritis, a type of kidney inflammation, can occur at any time during treatment. Symptoms include reduced urine output or blood in the urine. Contact your doctor immediately if these occur. 2. Antibiotic-Associated Diarrhea: Overgrowth of Clostridioides difficile bacteria in the gut can lead to severe diarrhea, abdominal cramps, fever, or blood in the stool. Seek medical attention if these symptoms develop. 3. Severe Skin Reactions: Rare but serious conditions like Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) or Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN) can occur, presenting as painful red or purple skin that peels, blisters, or affects the eyes, mouth, or genitals. Stop the medication and seek emergency care if these symptoms arise. 4. Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS): This rare allergic reaction can affect multiple organs, including the liver, kidneys, and heart. Symptoms include rash, fever, swollen lymph nodes, shortness of breath, and jaundice. Discontinue the medication and seek immediate medical help if these occur. 5. Bone Loss and Fractures: Long-term use, especially in older adults or at high doses, may increase the risk of bone fractures. 6. Hypomagnesemia: Prolonged use can lead to low magnesium levels, which may cause seizures, muscle spasms, dizziness, or irregular heart rhythms. Notify your doctor if you experience these symptoms. 7. Vitamin B12 Deficiency: Long-term use (over three years) may reduce vitamin B12 absorption, leading to symptoms like a sore tongue, weakness, or tingling in the hands and feet. Allergic Reactions: Lansoprazole can cause serious allergic reactions, including swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, difficulty breathing, hives, or dizziness. Stop the medication and seek emergency care if these symptoms occur. Precautions: Do not use lansoprazole if you are allergic to it, other proton pump inhibitors, or any of its ingredients. Inform your healthcare provider about all medications, supplements, and health conditions before starting lansoprazole. Avoid use during breastfeeding, as the medication can pass into breast milk. The safety of lansoprazole during pregnancy is not fully established. Consult your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Drug Interactions: Lansoprazole may interact with certain medications, including methotrexate, digoxin, warfarin, theophylline, clarithromycin, tacrolimus, antiretroviral drugs (e.g., rilpivirine, nelfinavir), St. John’s Wort, and rifampin. Always inform your healthcare provider about all medications and supplements you are taking. Usage Instructions: Take lansoprazole as prescribed, typically before meals. Do not chew, crush, or cut the capsules. If swallowing is difficult, the capsule contents can be sprinkled on a tablespoon of applesauce or yogurt and consumed immediately. Lansoprazole is not intended for immediate relief of heartburn and may take 1 to 4 days to take full effect. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember unless it is close to the next scheduled dose. Do not double doses. Storage: Store lansoprazole at room temperature (68°F to 77°F or 20°C to 25°C). Overdose: In case of an overdose, seek immediate medical attention, call 911, or contact a poison control center at 800-222-1222. Lansoprazole is available in various forms, including 15 mg and 30 mg delayed-release capsules and orally disintegrating tablets. Always follow your healthcare provider’s instructions for safe and effective use.
